newsitem.title: CANADA: Wascana board to decide on Talisman access.
newsitem.headline: Wascana board to decide on Talisman access.

text.p: Wascana Energy Inc's board of directors had yet to decide whether to allow Talisman Energy Inc access to its data room in the wake of Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd's richer takeover offer, Wascana chief executive Frank Proto said on Tuesday.

"There has been no decision," Proto said in a telephone interview from Regina. "What's normal in this kinds of cases is when a superior proposal comes, the directors...have to look at the considerations, and if that's one of the considerations, they're going to have to look at it."

He would not elaborate on what terms Talisman would have to meet before gaining access to Wascana's confidential financial and operating data. But Proto said he believed Talisman chief executive Jim Buckee "knows what the rules are."
CanOxy on Tuesday launched a C$2-billion competing takeover bid for Wascana, offering C$20.50 cash per share. CanOxy's proposal gained the blessing of Wascana's directors.
Talisman had earlier offered C$18.50 or 0.41 or a Talisman share for each Wascana share in a deal valued at C$1.7 billion.
Proto said he believed CanOxy's operations fit better with Wascana than Talisman's and that the white knight had more experience with heavy oil production in Saskatchewan.

He said he felt somewhat vindicated after CanOxy chief executive David Hentschel outlined in a conference call earlier how his firm's own evaluation of Wascana's reserves were similar to Wascana's controversial Ryder Scott Co tally.
Talisman had criticized the Ryder Scott report for its aggressive increases to Wascana's oil and gas reserves, especially at the company's Smiley-Buffalo heavy oil play in west-central Saskatchewan.
Proto said the emergence of a white knight and the higher offer were bittersweet from his personal standpoint, because Wascana's turnaround was well under way.
"I would have rather had other options," he said. "I'm proud of what we've done here, but I'm glad that the value's been recognized."
